description: Dynamically adjust chunk size for speculative parallel parsing based on local entropy of the JSON input. High-entropy regions (dense strings) use larger chunks to amortize speculation overhead; low-entropy regions (repeated structure) use smaller chunks for finer parallelism. Borrowed from adaptive compression algorithms that adjust window sizes based on source entropy.
mathematical_formalization: Local entropy: H(C_i) = -sum_b p(b) log p(b). Optimal chunk size: L_opt(H) = L_min * 2^(alpha * H / H_max). Speculation miss rate: P_miss ~ f_string * (1 - e^{-L/lambda}) where lambda = avg string length. Minimize: argmin_L { n/(L*P) * T_chunk + n/L * P_miss(L) * T_fixup }.
analogical_connections: Adaptive Huffman coding: adjust code tables based on symbol frequencies
TCP congestion window: dynamically size transmission window based on conditions
Adaptive mesh refinement in CFD: refine grid where solution has high gradients
implementation_hypothesis: First pass: scan at 4KB granularity computing byte frequency histograms using VPOPCNT. Compute entropy per block. Group blocks into variable-sized chunks with boundaries at low-entropy points. Feed to speculative parallel indexer. Grouping overhead: O(n/4096), SIMD-accelerable.
experiment_seed: Profile speculation miss rates as function of chunk size across different JSON files. Fit P_miss(L) model. Implement entropy-adaptive chunking. Compare against fixed-size. Target: >50% reduction in speculation misses on heterogeneous JSON.
